meaning: Inventory of metadata and implemented bounds; no inference that every field or source claim has been independently verified.

fields.label: Deployment package
fields.help: Choose a ZIP archive or container image; the supported runtime/handler settings differ.

fields.label: Runtime
fields.help: Record a currently supported runtime identifier. Runtime availability/deprecation must be checked for the selected Region and date.

fields.label: Handler
fields.help: For ZIP runtimes, identify the module and handler method using the runtime-specific format.

fields.label: Instruction set architecture
fields.help: Match the function architecture to native libraries, layers and the deployment artifact.

fields.label: Memory
fields.help: Memory also controls allocated CPU. Tune with measured workload behavior rather than assuming the smallest value is cheapest.

awsLimit.description: Function memory setting is 128–10,240 MB; account profiles can have lower effective quotas.

fields.label: Timeout
fields.help: The invocation deadline is not a guarantee that downstream side effects are rolled back.

awsLimit.description: 1–900 seconds for the ordinary Lambda Event Function modeled here. Other Lambda compute modes have different limits.

fields.label: Ephemeral storage (/tmp)
fields.help: Temporary encrypted scratch space is not durable application storage.

fields.label: Environment variables
fields.help: Use non-secret environment-specific values. Store references to secrets rather than literal credentials.

fields.label: Execution role
fields.help: The execution role is assumed by Lambda to access downstream AWS APIs. It does not grant a caller permission to invoke the function.

fields.label: Function resource-based policy
fields.help: Allow specified principals/services to invoke the correct function, version or alias; scope SourceArn/SourceAccount as applicable.

fields.label: Environment encryption key
fields.help: Distinguish environment-at-rest encryption and application-side KMS calls; evaluate each relevant principal.

fields.label: Layers
fields.help: ZIP functions can attach compatible layer versions. Check runtime, architecture and dependency precedence.

fields.label: Layer version ARN
fields.help: Use an explicit version reference; do not put secrets here.

fields.label: Dependency purpose
fields.help: Explain why the function needs this layer.

fields.label: SnapStart
fields.help: For supported runtimes/Regions, published-version snapshots can reduce initialization latency. Check compatibility with provisioned concurrency and uniqueness-sensitive initialization.

fields.label: Extensions
fields.help: Record required runtime extensions and compatibility; extensions consume function resources.

fields.label: Container image URI/digest
fields.help: Use an ECR image reference compatible with Lambda; identify a deployable immutable artifact.

fields.label: Image command/entrypoint/working directory
fields.help: Record image configuration overrides separately from ZIP runtime/handler settings.

fields.label: VPC attachment
fields.help: VPC attachment permits access to private resources; it does not itself supply internet access.

fields.label: Subnets and security groups
fields.help: Identify intended subnets/security-group references and outbound reachability, including access to AWS APIs.

fields.label: Subnet reference
fields.help: Use a configured subnet identifier, not an assertion that the subnet exists.

fields.label: Security group reference
fields.help: Record a security group with the required application egress.

fields.label: EFS mounts
fields.help: Record access point and mount path, then consider VPC, network and file permissions.

fields.label: EFS resource
fields.help: Choose a filesystem/access point represented by the workspace.

fields.label: Local mount path
fields.help: Record the Lambda mount directory.

fields.label: Reserved concurrency
fields.help: Reserves and caps concurrency for this function. It is different from pre-initialized capacity.

awsLimit.description: Available reservation depends on the account/Region concurrency quota and unreserved allocation.

fields.label: Provisioned concurrency
fields.help: Attach pre-initialized capacity to a version/alias; compare measured cold-start requirements and cost.

fields.label: Invocation path
fields.help: Retry, batching and error controls depend on the actual invocation path, not just the arrow direction.

fields.label: Event source mappings
fields.help: Configure a supported poll-based source, batching, filtering and failure behavior; settings differ by source.

fields.label: Event source
fields.help: Choose the source resource, not a push destination.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.help: Whether the mapping is enabled.

fields.label: Batch size
fields.help: Use the source-specific supported range.

audit.scope: Batch size: integer 1–10000; source-specific limits can be lower.

fields.label: Batching window
fields.help: Account for the batching window when coordinating queue visibility.

audit.scope: Batching window: integer 0–300 seconds; applicability also depends on event source.

fields.label: Report batch item failures
fields.help: Requires matching handler response logic; a checkbox does not implement the code.

fields.label: Filter criteria
fields.help: Specify the event-source-specific filter JSON.

fields.label: Starting position
fields.help: Relevant to stream mappings; not an SQS option.

fields.label: Maximum concurrency
fields.help: Source-dependent mapping concurrency control.

fields.label: Asynchronous maximum event age
fields.help: Maximum time an asynchronous event may wait for processing; does not apply to SQS polling.

fields.label: Asynchronous retry attempts
fields.help: Configure asynchronous invocation retries separately from SDK retries or SQS redrive.

fields.label: Asynchronous destinations
fields.help: Choose supported on-success/on-failure destinations and grant delivery permissions.

fields.label: Condition
fields.help: When the invocation record is sent.

fields.label: Destination resource
fields.help: Verify supported destination/service combinations; S3 is on-failure only, while SQS/SNS asynchronous destinations require standard resources.

fields.label: Asynchronous dead-letter target
fields.help: An asynchronous Lambda DLQ differs from a source SQS queue redrive DLQ.

fields.label: Idempotency strategy
fields.help: Describe the idempotency key, persistence and replay handling for operations that can be retried.

fields.label: Versions and aliases
fields.help: Publish immutable versions and point callers at aliases; weighted aliases support gradual release.

fields.label: Alias name
fields.help: Stable name used by callers.

fields.label: Published version
fields.help: A version reference; $LATEST is not an immutable published version.

fields.label: Additional version traffic weight
fields.help: Record the fractional traffic allocation.

fields.label: Additional version
fields.help: The version receiving the additional weight.

fields.label: Log group
fields.help: Choose log retention, access and sensitive-data controls on the log group.

fields.label: Log format
fields.help: Structured JSON supports consistent fields; redact secrets and input documents.

fields.label: Application log level
fields.help: Use supported logging controls and runtime/library behavior; log level names vary by runtime.

fields.label: X-Ray tracing
fields.help: Active tracing requires appropriate permissions and instrumentation for downstream calls.

fields.label: Operational alarms
fields.help: Define failure/throttle/duration/concurrency signals and the response/rollback decision.

fields.label: Metric
fields.help: Choose a documented metric and dimensions.

fields.label: Threshold/evaluation
fields.help: Describe the threshold, statistic and evaluation period.

fields.label: Notification target
fields.help: Where the alert is sent.

fields.label: API type
fields.help: Choose the API product first. Feature availability and authorization models are not interchangeable.

fields.label: Endpoint type
fields.help: Edge-optimized and private API endpoints are REST API features; private backend integration is a different concept.

fields.label: Backend integration family
fields.help: Choose the backend family; product-specific integration type and permissions still apply.

fields.label: Routes and integrations
fields.help: Define each route/method separately, including the backend target and product-specific integration.

fields.label: Route key / resource and method
fields.help: For HTTP API use a route key such as POST /summarize; REST uses a resource path plus method.

fields.label: Backend resource
fields.help: A graph reference identifies intent, not a deployed endpoint.

fields.label: HTTP URI / integration ARN
fields.help: Use a synthetic/documented reference when the actual deployment value is unknown.

fields.label: Integration type
fields.help: Validate supported types for the selected API product.

fields.label: Payload format
fields.help: Payload 2.0 is relevant to HTTP API Lambda proxy integration, not a universal REST setting.

fields.label: Authorizer reference
fields.help: Reference the authorizer configured for this route.

fields.label: API key required
fields.help: REST usage-plan API keys are not a replacement for authentication.

fields.label: HTTP API authorization
fields.help: Use JWT for supported OIDC/Cognito access tokens; CUSTOM denotes a Lambda authorizer.

fields.label: REST API authorization
fields.help: REST has Cognito user-pool and Lambda authorizers; JWT authorizer is not the native REST API authorizer type.

fields.label: Authorizers
fields.help: Configure the issuer/audience/scopes or Lambda authorizer and relevant identity sources.

fields.label: Authorizer name
fields.help: Reference this name from routes.

fields.label: Authorizer type
fields.help: Availability depends on API type.

fields.label: Identity source
fields.help: Typically the Authorization header; do not store tokens here.

fields.label: JWT issuer
fields.help: For JWT authorizers, require the intended issuer.

fields.label: JWT audience/client IDs
fields.help: Expected audience or application client IDs.

fields.label: Route authorization scopes
fields.help: Scopes are route-level requirements; validate access-token use.

fields.label: Lambda authorizer
fields.help: Use the correct function and invocation permission.

fields.label: Authorizer cache TTL
fields.help: Caching behavior depends on authorizer/API type.

fields.label: REST API resource policy
fields.help: Resource policies apply to REST APIs; they are not an HTTP API feature.

fields.label: Integration credentials role
fields.help: Some AWS service/private integrations need an assumed role. Distinguish this from Lambda resource-based invocation permission.

fields.label: CORS configuration
fields.help: Configure allowed origins, methods and headers for browser requests. CORS is not authentication.

fields.label: Allowed origin
fields.help: Use intended scheme/host/port, or explain any public wildcard.

fields.label: Allowed methods
fields.help: Include the intended method and preflight behavior.

fields.label: Allowed headers
fields.help: Include required content and authorization headers.

fields.label: Allow credentials
fields.help: Credentialed CORS and wildcard origin must be assessed together.

fields.label: Preflight cache age
fields.help: Browser cache duration.

fields.label: Stages and deployment
fields.help: Associate routes with an environment/deployment; do not assume all products use automatic deployment.

fields.label: Stage name
fields.help: Include $default only where the selected product supports it.

fields.label: Automatic deployment
fields.help: Supported by HTTP APIs, not a universal REST stage feature.

fields.label: Stage variables
fields.help: Store non-secret configuration references.

fields.label: Deployment reference
fields.help: Record the intended immutable deployment snapshot.

fields.label: Stage/route throttling
fields.help: Record supported rate/burst overrides and consider service/account quotas.

fields.label: Route or method
fields.help: Identify the scope of the override.

fields.label: Rate limit
fields.help: Requests per second in the intended configuration.

fields.label: Burst limit
fields.help: Token-bucket burst setting, not a billing cap.

fields.label: Usage plans and API-key associations
fields.help: REST usage plans provide consumer metering/throttling; API keys are not user authentication.

fields.label: Plan name
fields.help: Logical plan identifier.

fields.label: API-key reference
fields.help: Use an identifier, never a real API-key value.

fields.label: Quota
fields.help: Declared usage-plan request quota.

fields.label: Quota period
fields.help: Usage-plan quota period.

fields.label: Request validation
fields.help: REST APIs can validate declared body/parameters. This does not replace application validation.

fields.label: Request models / JSON schemas
fields.help: Declare request body shape and associate models with appropriate content types.

fields.label: Request/response parameter mappings
fields.help: Use product-appropriate mapping syntax and supported parameters.

fields.label: Body mapping templates
fields.help: REST mapping templates can transform bodies; HTTP API parameter mapping is not the same feature.

fields.label: Content type
fields.help: For example application/json.

fields.label: Velocity template
fields.help: Use a small educational template; the app does not execute arbitrary VTL.

fields.label: Stage/method cache
fields.help: REST stage caching requires explicit cache-key, TTL and invalidation decisions; HTTP APIs do not support this cache feature.

fields.label: Cache TTL
fields.help: Cache only responses safe for the chosen cache key and caller context.

fields.label: Private integration VPC link
fields.help: A private integration reaches a supported private backend; it does not make the API endpoint private.

fields.label: Private backend load balancer
fields.help: Reference a compatible listener/target group and network access configuration.

fields.label: Integration timeout
fields.help: Supported deadlines depend on API/integration type and applicable quota increases. Do not use the Lambda timeout as a proxy.

awsLimit.description: API product, integration and account/Region dependent; verify current integration timeout documentation.

fields.label: Error response strategy
fields.help: Map safe status/error responses; do not expose stack traces, prompts or credentials.

fields.label: Access logging
fields.help: Record safe request metadata; avoid full authorization headers and sensitive payloads.

fields.label: Log destination
fields.help: Use a supported destination for the API product.

fields.label: Log format
fields.help: Prefer safe structured identifiers, status, latency and error metadata.

fields.label: Execution logging
fields.help: REST execution logs differ from access logs; enable data tracing only with a sensitive-data review.

fields.label: X-Ray tracing
fields.help: REST API X-Ray tracing is not an HTTP API feature.

fields.label: Custom domain / certificate reference
fields.help: Specify domain, compatible certificate Region and API mapping; do not invent certificate ARNs.

fields.label: WAF web ACL
fields.help: Associate only where supported by the selected API product; HTTP API does not support direct WAF association.

fields.label: Synthetic request event
fields.help: Use a non-sensitive request to exercise the intended route, auth and payload shape.

fields.label: WebSocket route selection and connection handling
fields.help: For WebSocket APIs, define $connect/$disconnect/custom routes, authorization entry point and connection management separately from HTTP routes.

fields.label: Table name
fields.help: Use a logical table name with a defined application ownership boundary.

fields.label: Key attribute definitions
fields.help: Define scalar types for attributes used in table/index keys; do not predeclare every document attribute.

fields.label: Attribute name
fields.help: Key attribute name.

fields.label: Attribute type
fields.help: Key attributes use String, Number or Binary.

fields.label: Partition key
fields.help: Choose the key attribute used by required access patterns; consider key cardinality and traffic distribution.

fields.label: Sort key
fields.help: Optional table sort key enables ordered queries within a partition key.

fields.label: Global secondary indexes
fields.help: Model each GSI key/projection/capacity separately. GSI reads do not support strong consistency.

fields.label: Index name
fields.help: Unique index identifier.

fields.label: Partition key
fields.help: Can differ from the base-table key.

fields.label: Sort key
fields.help: Optional GSI sort key.

fields.label: Projection
fields.help: Balance query coverage with storage/write cost.

fields.label: Included non-key attributes
fields.help: Relevant to INCLUDE projection.

fields.label: Provisioned read units
fields.help: Only applicable to provisioned capacity.

fields.label: Provisioned write units
fields.help: Only applicable to provisioned capacity.

fields.label: Local secondary indexes
fields.help: LSIs share the table partition key and must be created with the table; they cannot be added/removed later.

fields.label: Index name
fields.help: Unique index identifier.

fields.label: Alternate sort key
fields.help: Shares the base-table partition key.

fields.label: Projection
fields.help: Projected attributes available from the index.

fields.label: Included attributes
fields.help: Relevant to INCLUDE projection.

fields.label: Capacity mode
fields.help: On-demand and provisioned capacity have different planning and throttling controls.

fields.label: Table provisioned read capacity
fields.help: Applicable only to provisioned mode; consider consistency and item sizes.

fields.label: Table provisioned write capacity
fields.help: Applicable only to provisioned mode; indexes also consume write capacity.

fields.label: Provisioned capacity auto scaling
fields.help: Capacity adaptation does not eliminate all throttling and hot-key concerns.

fields.label: Read consistency
fields.help: Strong reads are supported for table/LSI reads, not GSI or Streams reads.

fields.label: Read target
fields.help: Use the target type when evaluating consistency and permission requirements.

fields.label: Read operation
fields.help: Query requires a partition-key condition; filtering is not a substitute for an efficient key condition.

fields.label: Query key-condition example
fields.help: Use expression syntax, attribute-name aliases and typed values for an educational query.

fields.label: Conditional-write example
fields.help: Protect invariants/idempotency with the appropriate condition; a read followed by an unconditional write can race.

fields.label: Transaction example
fields.help: Use transactions for a bounded atomic application operation; reason about retries and idempotency tokens.

fields.label: Pagination handling
fields.help: Continue with LastEvaluatedKey/ExclusiveStartKey when present; one response is not necessarily the whole result.

fields.label: TTL attribute
fields.help: Use an epoch-seconds attribute and account for asynchronous deletion rather than treating TTL as an immediate authorization boundary.

fields.label: Stream view type
fields.help: Choose only the record data consumers need; Streams and Lambda processing require source-specific retry/filter settings.

fields.label: Stream consumer
fields.help: Configure event-source mapping and least-privilege stream-read permissions separately.

fields.label: Encryption key
fields.help: Table encryption and application data permissions are separate controls.

fields.label: Table/stream resource policy
fields.help: Constrain supported principals/actions/resources; cross-account and service-specific exceptions require context.

fields.label: Application role
fields.help: Scope table and index ARN permissions to the actual SDK operations.

fields.label: Point-in-time recovery
fields.help: Use recovery controls appropriate for important application data; this does not undo arbitrary application side effects.

fields.label: Retry and unprocessed items
fields.help: Apply bounded backoff and handle UnprocessedKeys/UnprocessedItems; blind retries can amplify contention.

fields.label: Caching/DAX strategy
fields.help: State cache consistency, invalidation and failure behavior; DAX is not a generic cache for every operation.

fields.label: Table/index monitoring
fields.help: Use consumed capacity, throttling, latency and errors with correct resource dimensions.

fields.label: Metric
fields.help: Documented DynamoDB metric.

fields.label: Table/index scope
fields.help: Match dimensions to the intended resource.

fields.label: Threshold
fields.help: Explain the condition and operational response.

fields.label: Bucket name
fields.help: Apply current bucket-type/namespace naming rules; a valid name is not proof it is available.

fields.label: Bucket type
fields.help: The DVA core profile models general-purpose buckets. Directory bucket capabilities, endpoints and permissions differ.

fields.label: Object Ownership
fields.help: Bucket owner enforced disables ACLs. Do not present ACL grants as effective in that mode.

fields.label: Block public ACLs
fields.help: Block new public ACLs; evaluate with the other block-public-access controls.

fields.label: Ignore public ACLs
fields.help: Ignore existing public ACLs without implying that all other access paths are denied.

fields.label: Block public bucket policies
fields.help: Reject applicable public policies; account-level controls can also restrict access.

fields.label: Restrict public buckets
fields.help: Evaluate public-policy restrictions with account and bucket context.

fields.label: Bucket policy
fields.help: Use bucket ARN for bucket operations and object ARN patterns for object operations; reason about explicit deny and conditions.

fields.label: Access control list
fields.help: ACLs have a distinct structure and are not IAM JSON policies; only model them when Object Ownership permits ACLs.

fields.label: Default encryption
fields.help: Default server-side encryption and permissions to use a KMS key are distinct; client-side encryption is an application choice.

fields.label: KMS key
fields.help: Select the intended KMS key and account for key policy plus principal permissions.

fields.label: S3 Bucket Key
fields.help: Check compatibility with the chosen encryption mode; this changes KMS request behavior, not object access authorization.

fields.label: Versioning
fields.help: Suspension is not the same as deleting prior object versions.

fields.label: Lifecycle rules
fields.help: Separate current/noncurrent transitions, expiration and incomplete multipart cleanup. Consider minimum storage duration and supported transitions.

fields.label: Rule ID
fields.help: Unique descriptive rule ID.

fields.label: Prefix filter
fields.help: Object-key prefix included in the rule.

fields.label: Tag filter
fields.help: Objects must match intended tag conditions.

fields.label: Current-version transition age
fields.help: Age before the configured transition.

fields.label: Transition storage class
fields.help: Verify current transition constraints for size and age.

fields.label: Current-version expiration
fields.help: Deletion action after the intended age.

fields.label: Noncurrent-version expiration
fields.help: Requires version-aware lifecycle reasoning.

fields.label: Abort incomplete multipart uploads
fields.help: Cleanup window for incomplete uploads.

fields.label: Object Lock
fields.help: Object Lock protects object versions and requires versioning; distinguish retention from legal hold.

fields.label: Object retention mode
fields.help: Governance and compliance have different bypass/change behavior.

fields.label: Default retention period
fields.help: A configured period must reflect the data-retention requirement, not a guessed exam default.

fields.label: Event notifications
fields.help: Use supported event types, prefix/suffix filtering and destination permissions. Delivery may be duplicated or reordered.

fields.label: Notification ID
fields.help: Identify the configuration.

fields.label: Event types
fields.help: For example s3:ObjectCreated:*; verify the event family.

fields.label: Prefix
fields.help: Filter object key prefixes.

fields.label: Suffix
fields.help: Filter object key suffixes.

fields.label: Destination
fields.help: Check destination type, Region and permission requirements.

fields.label: Send events to EventBridge
fields.help: EventBridge delivery is a distinct bucket notification setting.

fields.label: CORS rules
fields.help: Browser CORS settings do not grant object permissions.

fields.label: Allowed origins
fields.help: Limit origins to intended frontends.

fields.label: Allowed methods
fields.help: Use only S3-supported CORS methods.

fields.label: Allowed request headers
fields.help: Include needed signed headers.

fields.label: Exposed response headers
fields.help: Only expose application-required response metadata.

fields.label: Preflight cache
fields.help: Browser cache duration.

fields.label: Presigned operations
fields.help: A presigned request uses the signing principal authority; expiry cannot outlive the signing credentials.

fields.label: Operation
fields.help: Choose the intended object operation.

fields.label: Object key
fields.help: Use synthetic keys, not confidential object paths.

fields.label: Requested expiration
fields.help: Compare with credential expiry and the signing method.

fields.label: Required headers/constraints
fields.help: Record content type/checksum or POST policy constraints as applicable.

fields.label: Multipart upload strategy
fields.help: Track upload ID/part numbers, complete or abort correctly and consider required permissions.

fields.label: Replication rules
fields.help: Consider versioning, destination ownership, replication role, encryption and existing-object behavior. Live replication differs from Batch Replication.

fields.label: Rule ID
fields.help: Rule identifier.

fields.label: Destination bucket
fields.help: Choose destination bucket/Region.

fields.label: Replication role
fields.help: Grant source/destination and applicable KMS permissions.

fields.label: Object filter
fields.help: Select the object prefix/tags covered by the rule.

fields.label: Replicate delete markers
fields.help: Use the documented rule-specific behavior.

fields.label: Transfer Acceleration
fields.help: Check endpoint and bucket-name compatibility; it is not always a cost/performance benefit.

fields.label: Private application access
fields.help: Gateway/interface endpoint paths and endpoint policies differ; a private path does not itself grant object access.

fields.label: Server access log destination
fields.help: Use a supported logging destination and safe retention/access controls.

fields.label: CloudTrail data-event scope
fields.help: Object data events require explicit event selectors; do not assume management-event history records every GetObject.

fields.label: Retries and checksums
fields.help: Use SDK retry behavior, checksum validation and idempotent object-key/version handling; do not log payloads.

fields.label: S3 bucket
fields.help: Glacier storage classes belong to S3 objects; do not model this as an unrelated online key-value database.

fields.label: Archive storage class
fields.help: Instant Retrieval, Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive have different access/retrieval behavior.

fields.label: Access/retrieval requirement
fields.help: State how quickly archived data must be available and how often it is read.

fields.label: Restore retrieval tier
fields.help: Availability depends on the archive class; not every class supports every retrieval tier.

fields.label: Temporary restored copy lifetime
fields.help: Relevant for archive classes restored to a temporary readable copy, not Glacier Instant Retrieval.

fields.label: Lifecycle transition age
fields.help: Verify class-specific transition/minimum-duration constraints rather than guessing a common number.

fields.label: Encryption key
fields.help: Preserve access to encryption keys for the full archive lifetime.

fields.label: Restore/read permissions
fields.help: Distinguish RestoreObject from GetObject and required KMS permissions.

fields.label: Retention and deletion policy
fields.help: Storage billing minimums, retention requirements and Object Lock are different constraints.

fields.label: Restore completion notifications
fields.help: Use supported S3 event notifications to detect restore completion; do not poll as though restore were always immediate.

fields.label: Queue type
fields.help: Standard queues can duplicate/reorder messages. FIFO ordering is per message group, not unlimited global throughput.

fields.label: Queue name
fields.help: FIFO queue names require the .fifo suffix. Account/Region ownership determines uniqueness.

fields.label: Visibility timeout
fields.help: Time a received message is hidden; it is not the same as retention or receive wait.

awsLimit.description: Maximum visibility timeout is 12 hours from receipt; extending it does not reset that maximum.

fields.label: Receive wait time
fields.help: Long polling waits for messages before returning; coordinate the HTTP client timeout.

fields.label: Maximum message size
fields.help: The API parameter is in bytes. The queue limit is separate from Lambda payload/batch limits.

fields.label: Message retention
fields.help: Retaining messages does not prevent duplicate processing or authorize access.

fields.label: Delivery delay
fields.help: Delay before messages become available. Per-message timers are not supported for FIFO queues.

fields.label: Dead-letter queue
fields.help: Use a compatible queue type and deliberate retention; moving FIFO messages to a DLQ can break end-to-end ordering.

fields.label: Maximum receive count
fields.help: How often the source queue permits receipt before redrive to its configured DLQ.

fields.label: DLQ redrive allow policy
fields.help: Specify which source queues may use this queue as a DLQ. This differs from the source queue redrive policy.

fields.label: Queue access policy
fields.help: Scope producer/consumer/service principals and SourceArn/SourceAccount conditions as required.

fields.label: Encryption
fields.help: KMS encryption can require additional producer/consumer and service key permissions.

fields.label: KMS key
fields.help: Choose an appropriate key and account for encrypted source/DLQ access.

fields.label: Message group strategy
fields.help: Partition related work into message groups; concurrent groups can progress independently.

fields.label: Content-based deduplication
fields.help: FIFO deduplication uses the message body hash when enabled; message attributes are not included in that hash.

fields.label: Deduplication ID strategy
fields.help: Define stable IDs for retried sends; deduplication is not a replacement for application idempotency.

fields.label: Deduplication scope
fields.help: High-throughput FIFO settings require a compatible deduplication scope.

fields.label: FIFO throughput limit
fields.help: Configure together with deduplication scope and verify current throughput quotas.

fields.label: Lambda consumer
fields.help: Lambda polls through an event-source mapping; this is not Lambda asynchronous invocation.

fields.label: Consumer batch size
fields.help: Batch size limits differ for standard/FIFO queues and consumer APIs; use source-specific limits.

audit.scope: Lambda consumer batch size: up to 10000 for standard queues, 10 for FIFO (checked separately).

fields.label: Lambda batch window
fields.help: A batching window changes effective waiting time and must be included in queue-visibility reasoning.

audit.scope: Lambda batching window: integer 0–300 seconds; FIFO SQS does not support a batching window.

fields.label: Partial batch response
fields.help: Requires correct Lambda response code; only retry failed records while respecting FIFO ordering.

fields.label: Lambda mapping maximum concurrency
fields.help: Coordinate mapping concurrency and function reserved concurrency to avoid throttling.

fields.label: Idempotent consumer
fields.help: Declare a concrete idempotency strategy; queue semantics alone do not guarantee side-effect exactly-once processing.

fields.label: Receipt-handle handling
fields.help: Delete/change visibility using the current receipt handle, not the message ID.

fields.label: Queue monitoring
fields.help: Watch age, backlog, in-flight messages and DLQ arrivals; explain scaling/recovery actions.

fields.label: Metric
fields.help: Use the correct approximate queue metric.

fields.label: Threshold/evaluation
fields.help: Choose a threshold that reflects application latency goals.

fields.label: Notification target
fields.help: Alert destination.

fields.label: Topic type
fields.help: Select supported ordering/delivery behavior and compatible subscription targets.

fields.label: Topic name
fields.help: Use .fifo suffix for FIFO topics and identify application ownership.

fields.label: Subscriptions
fields.help: Fan-out configuration belongs to each subscription, including endpoint, confirmation, filtering and delivery behavior.

fields.label: Protocol
fields.help: Supported protocols depend on topic type and endpoint service.

fields.label: Workspace destination
fields.help: Prefer graph references for modeled AWS resources.
